subject: DPA redlines — retention, backup phase-out & egress clarifications
messages:
From: Julie Park <julie.park@acmehealth.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA redlines — retention & egress questions

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. We reviewed Redwood's DPA and have several redlines and clarifying questions from legal and infosec before we can proceed:

1) Backups: our policy requires that backups holding customer data be removable within 30 days of a deletion request. Your DPA currently references a 90-day restore window for backups. Is that an absolute or can we limit backup retention containing customer PII to 30 days?

2) Transient transit/egress: we need explicit language that data for Acme Health EU customers remains resident in the EU and that any transient processing in the US is limited to <48 hours and only for routing/recovery. Current redline implies broader transits.

3) Incident forensics: infosec requests a 12-month forensic log retention for incident investigations; can you provide a scope list of which logs are kept and for how long?

4) Backup snapshots & cold archives: are archives subject to the same deletion trigger as the primary dataset? We saw an ambiguous clause.

Attached: Acme_DPA_redline_v3.pdf with our annotated suggestions. Please route to your product/legal folks and get us a counter-proposal. We are targeting signing the DPA before the end of October.

Julie Park
Legal Counsel — Privacy & Data
Acme Health

-- Attachment: Acme_DPA_redline_v3.pdf (annotated redlines)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Julie Park <julie.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — retention & egress questions

Julie — thanks for the clear list and the annotated PDF. Appreciate the target timeline; we'll move quickly. High-level responses inline, then next steps.

1) Backups: Redwood's standard position is a 90-day restore window for snapshot retention to support restores and compliance audits. That said, we can offer a carve for customer PII where the backup retention window is shortened to 30 days if the customer requires it and it is operationally feasible in the deployment (Dedicated/Private only). For Hosted customers, we can commit to purging PII from backups within 30 days for EU-region deployments, subject to a technical feasibility review.

2) Transit/egress: agree we should tighten language. We can add specific language: "Customer data assigned to an EU residency configuration will be stored in EU regions and will not be transferred outside the EU except for transient processing not to exceed 48 hours and only for routing, failover, or emergency recovery."

3) Forensic logs: we maintain different classes of logs. We can provide a labeled list: access logs (12 months), system-level telemetry (90 days), and high-fidelity audit trails for security incidents (12 months). I'll attach an extract of our DPA appendix that maps categories -> retention.

4) Archives: cold archives are treated as backups; by default the same deletion trigger applies but we can offer an appendix that allows Acme to opt for a shorter archive TTL on request.

Next steps: I attached a short extract from our DPA (redwood-dpa-extracts.docx) and a suggested set of compromise bullet points. I'll circulate to Markus (product/legal lead) and Dylan (security) for concrete counter-redlines and target to get a drafted counter-proposal back to you by EOD 2027-10-05.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Partner — Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com

-- Attachment: redwood-dpa-extracts.docx (excerpted appendix)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-03T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: RE: DPA redlines — retention & egress questions (internal)

Quick internal notes / proposed concessions for Acme: 

- Backups: Offer two tracks in the DPA: Hosted (standard 90-day), Dedicated/Private (30-day PII backup retention option). That keeps Hosted product economics intact while giving enterprise customers the control they need.

- Provide explicit "transient processing" sentence with a hard 48-hour cap and an explicit list of purposes (routing, failover, emergency incident response). Avoid open-ended "processing" language.

- For forensic logs: give them a table in the appendix. We can commit to 12 months for access/audit logs relevant to the Acme tenant, with the carve that logs retained for forensics are limited to metadata and not full payloads unless legally required.

- Archives: commit to enforce deletion triggers across live/backups/cold-archives where possible, but call out where immutable vendor snapshots or third-party backups may be subject to industry-standard retention and provide an SLA for purge attempts.

If legal is OK with the two-track approach we should be able to get them a clean counter-redline quickly. Suggest we attach a short "operational note" describing the restore/erase workflow so Acme's team understands the steps and timelines.

-- Attachment: redlines-suggested.txt
From: Julie Park <julie.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Security <infosec@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — retention & egress questions

Rachel / team — thank you for the prompt reply. The two-track approach is acceptable to Acme in principle; a few clarifications before we sign off: 

- Hosted vs Dedicated/Private: We plan to start on Hosted, but need the option to migrate to a Dedicated pool within 90 days without losing the 30-day PII backup retention commitment. Can you confirm the migration path preserves the shorter backup retention?

- Forensic logs: can you confirm the logs we would receive during an incident investigation are tenant-scoped and include request IDs, timestamps, and the model version used? We need these to satisfy our audit.

- SLA for purge attempts: can you provide target dates for purge attempts and a playbook if a vendor snapshot prevents deletion (e.g., escrow or court-ordered holds)?

If you can include those clarifications in the counter-redline we can fast-track review on our side. Also: we would like the counter-redline as a tracked Word doc so our legal team can add comments inline.

Julie Park
Legal Counsel — Privacy & Data
Acme Health
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Julie Park <julie.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-06T15:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — retention & egress questions — counter-redline attached

Julie — attached is our formal counter-redline (redwood-counter-redline.docx) and an operational playbook that addresses the migration path, tenant-scoped logs, and purge SLA. Highlights: 

- Migration: we will preserve the customer's chosen retention profile when migrating from Hosted -> Dedicated for the first 90 days post-migration; any change beyond 90 days requires 30 days' notice.

- Tenant-scoped logs: we commit to providing request IDs, timestamps, model version, and request/response metadata for 12 months for forensic investigations, subject to legal limitations on response payloads.

- Purge SLA: purge attempt timeline: initial purge attempt within 7 calendar days, follow-up escalation to 30 days if third-party snapshots are implicated; we will provide monthly status updates until purge completes. We also included language describing legal holds and how they interact with the purge timeline.

Please review the tracked doc; if that looks ok we can hand to our legal team for final review and then send a DocuSign package. Target for our side: legal sign-off by 2027-10-11 so you can execute before month-end.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk the playbook.

Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Partner — Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com

-- Attachment: redwood-counter-redline.docx (tracked changes)
